To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we developed a 5 W AlGaNGaN power amplifier MMICS operating between 25–27GHz, that is, a power amplifier for the 25–27-GHz downlink application.
we developed a 5 W GaN power amplifier that operates in CW mode with a peak PAE of over 35 % at 15 V drain supply voltage.
a GaN-based PA MMIC for the 26 GHz frequency band is designed and analyzed.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design, fabrication, and characterization of a 5-W AlGaN/Ga N HEMT power amplifier for 25-27 GHz.
the development of a 5W power amplifier MMIC in the Ka-band for downlink applications.
the development of a high-efficiency and high-output power PA MMIC for the downlink band of 26 GHz.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the MMIC presented in this work is an excellent candidate for the realization of a high power PA for 5G base station applications.
the presented 5 W PA MMIC is a very promising candidate for 25–26 GHz downlink applications, especially for satellite communication.
the MMIC presented here is the first 5 W AlGaNGaN HEMT MMIC in the 26 GHz band and that it is the highest power MMIC ever demonstrated in this frequency band.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a 5 W PA MMIC has been realized in the 0.15 µm AlGAN/GaN HEMTs technology.
a 5 W PA MMIC has been developed and characterized.
we were able to design a 26 GHz power amplifier MMIC with a power output of more than 4 W at 14 V drain supply voltage, and 30 % PAE.
The main takeaway from our work is that
GaN MMICs are suitable for high power operation at 26 GHz.
GaN technology is suitable for high-power and high-efficiency operation in the downlink frequency bands of 5G cellular systems.
GaN-based technology can be successfully employed for high-power applications around 26 GHz.
